rows.why: We expect about 3.7 catches vs the 4.0 line. We give the under 69% (needs 57% per pick on PrizePicks); recent games and the matchup both point lower
rows.why_long: PrizePicks lower 4.0 needs 57% per pick for your entry; fair view 70% (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.8 over the last 8 games, lower than 4.0 in 52% of them (raw 61%, shrunk 69%). Projects 3.7 (raw 64%, shrunk 69%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions lower 4.0 on PrizePicks. Each pick has to win 57% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 70%.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 2, 5, 3, 6, 5, 5, 4. Weighted average 3.8; went lower than 4.0 in 3 of 8 games (52% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 3.3 vs 4.6 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.3, so the line is 0.1 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — basically a coin flip.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -6% on his average.
PFF: BUF plays man on 25% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 29%); he gains 1.40 yds/route vs man and 1.63 vs zone → +1% from scheme.
PFF: BUF allows 1.45 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.59) → -10% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 50% of his routes from the slot (1.67 yds/route there, 1.28 outside); BUF allows 1.42 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.52 outside (league 1.54 / 1.62, opponent-adjusted) → -9% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 3.7 catches on average; in a typical game 3.3 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.7 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 61% and the matchup 64%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 69%, matchup 69%.
Bottom line: we give it 69% to win and it needs 57%. The edge is the difference: +12.2 points; that works out to about +21¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: The under looks good: we expect about 3.3 in a typical game vs the 4 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.
